messages.subject: Some questions
parts: I am new member of this mail list and I began to study distance sampling.

I would like to ask you a few things.
My doubst are basically the following.

1. In the book =93Distance Sampling=94 by Bockland et al (1993), g(y) is
modeled by g(y) =3D key(y) [ 1 + series(y) ] (that I am calling model 1)
and some functions for key(y) and series(y) are proposed.

In the case that key(y) is the uniform and series(y) is cosine, the
model is the series of Fourier. I tried to find the expression for g(y)
given in the book, but I didn=92t have success. I find the expression when

I use for g(y) the model given by g(y) =3D key(y) + series(y) (model 2).
Is it correct?
In which situation can I use model 1 and model 2?

Are there explicit forms for f(0) and Var [ f(0) ] for transect lines
and transect points?

3. I would like to know if someone has real data obtained by transect
lines and transect points and in positive case, I would like to know if
I could use this data.

Diana Milena Galvis
Ms Student at Statistics
IME - Institute of Mathematics and Statistics
USP - University of Sao Paulo

messages.subject: Re: Some questions
parts:
The formulation used for g(y) is g(y) =3D key(y) [ 1 + series(y) ] in bot=
h
the 1993 and 2001 Buckland et al books and in the software DISTANCE.=20
Then as you state f(y) =3D [g(y)] / [int(g(y))]. This differs from Burnha=
m
et al and the software TRANSECT which used the Fourier series which is
f(y) =3D key(y) + series(y), where key(y)=3D1/W and series(y) is the cosi=
ne
series for even functions. Strictly speaking, in the first case g(y) =3D
[key(y) [ 1 + series(y) ]]/[key(0) [ 1 + series(0)]] because g(0)=3D1 but
this is a minor detail because any non-unity g(0) value cancels out in
the formulation of f(y).

Except for simplistic cases (untruncated half-normal key function and
uniform key function) there are no explicit closed form equations for
f(0) and it variance. Everything in DISTANCE is computed by numerically
maximizing the likelihood function. The Fourier series implementation
in TRANSECT did have closed form equations.

--jeff
